classification.difficultyReason: Uses the nonnegative range of absolute value, then represents the same conclusion by sketching a translated V and a horizontal line with no intersections.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why the equation $|x+3|=-5$ has no solutions.

answer.short: An absolute value is nonnegative, so it cannot equal $-5$.
answer.worked: $|x+3|\geq0$ for every real $x$, whereas $-5<0$. Hence the equation has no solutions.

answer.short: The graphs $y=|x+3|$ and $y=-5$ do not intersect.
answer.worked: Sketch $y=|x+3|$, with vertex $(-3,0)$, and the horizontal line $y=-5$. The V-shaped graph lies on or above the $x$-axis, while the line lies below it. There are no intersections, so there are no solutions.

spec.description: Complete independently authored graphical justification; two distinguished functions and no intersections. No grid; coordinate units are explicit.
spec.mathematics: y=|x+3| has vertex (-3,0); y=-5 lies strictly below its range.
